import json, os

base = "/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-be-idea-gen-0519-4/projects/policy_ambiguity_safety/artifacts/full_study/judgments"
models = ["gpt-5.4", "gpt-4.1", "claude-sonnet-4-6", "deepseek-v3", "qwen3-235b"]

# Cross-judge map: GPT-5.4 judges Claude, GPT-4.1, Qwen3; GPT-4.1 judges GPT-5.4, DeepSeek
# So: OpenAI-judged = Claude, GPT-4.1, Qwen3 (judged by GPT-5.4) + GPT-5.4, DeepSeek (judged by GPT-4.1)
# Actually the question is about grouping by WHICH judge evaluates them
# OpenAI-judged models (judged by an OpenAI model): all 5 are judged by OpenAI models
# The Director's framing: compare models judged by GPT-5.4 vs models judged by GPT-4.1

# Per the cross-judge map:
# GPT-5.4 judges: claude-sonnet-4-6, gpt-4.1, qwen3-235b
# GPT-4.1 judges: gpt-5.4, deepseek-v3

# Build per-model violation sets (ambiguous condition only)
model_violations = {}
for model in models:
    jpath = os.path.join(base, model, "judgments.jsonl")
    violations = set()
    with open(jpath) as f:
        for line in f:
            d = json.loads(line)
            if d["condition"] == "ambiguous":
                vl = d["judgment"]["violation_level"]
                if vl in ("moderate", "critical"):
                    violations.add(d["clause_id"])
    model_violations[model] = violations

# Get all 300 clause IDs
all_clauses = set()
for v in model_violations.values():
    # We need all clause IDs, not just violations
    pass

# Re-read to get all ambiguous clause IDs
all_clause_ids = set()
for model in models:
    jpath = os.path.join(base, model, "judgments.jsonl")
    with open(jpath) as f:
        for line in f:
            d = json.loads(line)
            if d["condition"] == "ambiguous":
                all_clause_ids.add(d["clause_id"])

# Convergent = >=3/5 models violated
convergent_clauses = set()
for cid in all_clause_ids:
    count = sum(1 for m in models if cid in model_violations[m])
    if count >= 3:
        convergent_clauses.add(cid)

# Group 1: judged by GPT-5.4 (claude, gpt-4.1, qwen3)
group1_models = ["claude-sonnet-4-6", "gpt-4.1", "qwen3-235b"]
# Group 2: judged by GPT-4.1 (gpt-5.4, deepseek)
group2_models = ["gpt-5.4", "deepseek-v3"]

# Per-group violation rate on ambiguous clauses
for label, grp in [("GPT-5.4-judged (Claude, GPT-4.1, Qwen3)", group1_models),
                    ("GPT-4.1-judged (GPT-5.4, DeepSeek)", group2_models)]:
    total_viols = sum(len(model_violations[m]) for m in grp)
    total_possible = len(all_clause_ids) * len(grp)
    rate = total_viols / total_possible * 100
    print(f"{label}: {total_viols}/{total_possible} = {rate:.1f}%")

# Per-group convergent violation rate
# For each clause, count violations within each group
for label, grp in [("GPT-5.4-judged", group1_models), ("GPT-4.1-judged", group2_models)]:
    conv_count = 0
    threshold = len(grp) / 2  # majority within group
    for cid in all_clause_ids:
        count = sum(1 for m in grp if cid in model_violations[m])
        if count > threshold:
            conv_count += 1
    rate = conv_count / len(all_clause_ids) * 100
    print(f"{label} majority-convergent: {conv_count}/{len(all_clause_ids)} = {rate:.1f}%")

# Overall convergent rate for reference
print(f"\nOverall convergent (>=3/5): {len(convergent_clauses)}/{len(all_clause_ids)} = {len(convergent_clauses)/len(all_clause_ids)*100:.1f}%")

# Per-model violation counts
for m in models:
    print(f"  {m}: {len(model_violations[m])}/300 = {len(model_violations[m])/300*100:.1f}%")
EOF

Our taxonomy uses \emph{ambiguity} as a policy specification umbrella term encompassing two epistemologically distinct operations.
